about: Held-out probes for the hybrid on 6 papers never used in any earlier bench (downloaded 2026-10-30), written from each paper's pdftotext text (not its clause base, not any model answer) before any run, 2026-10-30. Fields span chemical engineering (Aspen transesterification, teak pyrolysis, condenser entrainment), animal nutrition, plant genomics and particle physics. cat: C lookup, B binding trap, T table, X computation, H chained lookup, K count, F false premise, A absence. expect cites pdftotext pages (p = PDF page). must: every group must occur in the answer (alternatives inside a group; NEG = any absence wording) - a triage aid only, every answer is graded by hand. Frozen by frozen.sha256 before the first run.

droplet.q: What share of the vapour does the surface air-cooled condenser process at the United Sugar Company refinery recover?
droplet.expect: 100% of the vapour, recycled back to process (p1, abstract)

droplet.q: Which type of separator does the paper conclude is most applicable for evaporators?
droplet.expect: the impingement separator (p1, conclusion); electrostatic and centrifugal are named as other types

droplet.q: What causes of entrainment of sugar solutions does the paper list, and what damage to the condenser can the entrainment cause?
droplet.expect: air leaks, unstable vacuum, foaming substances; scale formation, fouling, erosion and corrosion of the condenser's pipes and headers (p1, introduction)

droplet.q: Since separators sized for removal efficiencies above 99% guarantee a pure condensate, why does the paper still recommend a structured selection procedure?
droplet.expect: premise false: the paper says even >99% efficiency may not be enough to ensure pure condensate (p1, conclusion)

droplet.q: How many tonnes of sugar per year does the refinery lose to entrainment?
droplet.expect: not reported (keywords only mention 'unknown sugar loss')

nutrisigma.q: How many Garole lambs were used, how were they grouped, and how long did the growth trial last?
nutrisigma.expect: 18 lambs, 3 groups of 6 (control, T1, T2), 105 days (p1 abstract; p2 methods)

nutrisigma.q: What was the cost per kg of live weight gain in the T2 group?
What crude protein content does Table 1 give for the concentrate mixture?
nutrisigma.trap: the ~30% crude protein of DDGS (p2) or Nutrisigma's 80 g per 250 g

nutrisigma.q: Which group had the highest mean body weight on day 105, and what was it?
By what percentage was the cost per kg of gain in T1 lower than in the control group?
How much Nutrisigma did each T2 lamb eat over the whole trial, and what share of the T2 group's total ration cost was Nutrisigma?
nutrisigma.expect: 2.1 kg per head (p3); Rs. 231 of Rs. 703.50 = 32.8% (Table 4, p4)

nutrisigma.q: Which supplementation level do the authors conclude is economically most viable, and what final body condition score did that group reach?
nutrisigma.expect: 10 g/head/day (T1); final BCS 3.20 (from 2.65) (Table 4, p4; conclusion p5)

nutrisigma.q: Why did the control group's body condition score fall during the trial?
nutrisigma.expect: premise false: control BCS rose slightly, 2.70 to 2.72 (Table 4, p4; text p5)

nutrisigma.q: What dressing percentage did the T1 lambs have at slaughter?
nutrisigma.expect: not reported: no slaughter or carcass data (carcass appears only in reference titles)

teak-pyrolysis.q: What was the highest bio-oil yield, and at what temperature and residence time was it obtained?
teak-pyrolysis.expect: 38.41 wt% at 450 °C and 25 min (abstract p1; p3; conclusion p5)

teak-pyrolysis.q: What coefficient of determination (R²) did the bio-oil yield model have?
What hydrogen content do the teak tree leaves have, and how does it compare with tanjong leaves?
teak-pyrolysis.expect: teak 16.95% H vs tanjong 5.23% H (p3; Table 1)

teak-pyrolysis.q: What F-value does the ANOVA give for temperature in the bio-gas yield model?
What lower heating value does Table 1 give for the teak tree leaves?
What share of the bio-oil model's total sum of squares does temperature account for?
Which product's model had the lowest coefficient of variation, and at what temperature and residence time was that product's maximum yield obtained?
teak-pyrolysis.expect: bio-gas, C.V. 1.99%; maximum 40.27% at 500 °C and 30 min (p3-4; Table 3)

teak-pyrolysis.q: Why did the bio-oil yield keep rising all the way up to 500 °C?
teak-pyrolysis.expect: premise false: bio-oil rose from 300 to 450 °C, then decreased at 500 °C (p3)

teak-pyrolysis.q: What higher heating value did the bio-oil produced from the teak leaves have?
teak-pyrolysis.expect: not reported for the bio-oil; 19.34 MJ/kg is the leaves' HHV (Table 1)

teak-pyrolysis.q: What heating rate, in °C per minute, was used in the furnace?
teak-pyrolysis.trap: inventing a heating rate, or giving the 50 °C temperature steps

aspen-transest.q: What triolein conversion and FAME yield does Model 1 achieve at the optimum conditions?
aspen-transest.expect: 96.4% conversion; 7.46 kg/h FAME (~7.5 kg/h) (abstract; conclusion p11)

aspen-transest.q: What biodiesel yield did Harb et al. obtain from spent coffee ground oil, and at what methanol-to-oil ratio and temperature?
aspen-transest.expect: 90.31% yield, 12:1, 60 °C (p2); Table 11 lists Harb & Jaoudeh at 95% conversion

aspen-transest.q: What activation energy does Table 9 give for the TG to DG step in Model 5?
aspen-transest.expect: 74.5 kJ/mol (Table 9, p7); Model 4's TG to DG is 13.5 kcal/mol (Table 7)

aspen-transest.q: In Table 11, which study reports the highest conversion, and at what reaction temperature and methanol-to-oil ratio?
aspen-transest.expect: Gaurav et al. (2013): 99.38% at 160 °C, 9:1, 3 wt% CaO on Al2O3 (Table 11, p9)

aspen-transest.q: In the methanol-to-oil sensitivity study, by how many percentage points does conversion rise from 20:1 to 30:1, and from 30:1 to 40:1?
Which model gave the lowest conversion, whose kinetic parameters did it use, and what catalyst did it use?
aspen-transest.expect: Model 5 (21%); Singh and Ali; K+ impregnated H3PW12O40.xH2O on graphene oxide (potassium-imbued phosphotungstic acid) (Table 1; sec. 2.3.5; Table 10)

aspen-transest.q: Since Model 2 recovers the most FAME and also leaves the fewest impurities, why did the authors still prefer Model 1?
aspen-transest.expect: premise half false: Model 2 recovers most (99% vs 98%) but its biodiesel has 10x the methanol and 1.5x the glycerol of Model 1 (sec. 3.4, p9)
aspen-transest.trap: accepting that Model 2 has fewer impurities

aspen-transest.q: Why did conversion keep increasing as the reactor temperature was raised from 55 to 75 °C?
aspen-transest.expect: premise false: 96.4% at 55 and 65 °C, falling to 96.3% at 75 °C (sec. 3.6.2, p10)

aspen-transest.q: What payback period does the paper estimate for a plant based on Model 1?
aspen-transest.expect: not reported: techno-economic assessment is left as future work (sec. 4); payback periods mentioned belong to other studies
aspen-transest.trap: attributing another study's payback result to Model 1

agave.q: How large is the Agave angustifolia chloroplast genome, and how many annotated genes does it hold?
agave.expect: 157,274 bp; 132 genes (86 protein-coding, 38 tRNAs, 8 rRNAs) (Fig. 6 caption, p9)

agave.q: What range of global DNA methylation does the review report for somaclonal variants?
agave.expect: 30.5-40% GDM (Table 2, p12); the species in general 13-22%

agave.q: What share of the raicilla industry uses Agave angustifolia, and does it rank first?
agave.trap: calling A. angustifolia the most used

agave.q: According to Table 2, how many unigenes and how many SNPs are reported, and for which biological variants?
agave.trap: swapping, or the 'over 50,000 SNPs' of sec. 5.2

agave.q: What ploidy and what percentage of polymorphic loci does Table 1 give for the 'Espadín' cultivar?
agave.expect: diploid (2n = 60) and triploid (2n = 3x = 90); 95.8% polymorphic loci (Table 1, p5)

agave.q: What share of the chloroplast genome do the two inverted repeats make up together?
Which clonal line does the review single out as the most thermally resilient, what is it derived from, and what temperature is the physiological optimum for growth-related metabolism?
agave.expect: CL24b, derived from bulbils; optimum 35 °C (decline beyond 45 °C) (sec. 6.2, p12)

agave.q: Since intensive clonal management lowers heterozygosity in 'Espadín', how does the review propose to restore it?
agave.expect: premise false: 'Espadín' has reduced total variability but a higher proportion of heterozygous genotypes (HO > HE) (p5, sec. 5.2, p18)

agave.q: Why does nocturnal CO2 fixation supply only about a quarter of Agave angustifolia's daily carbon gain?
agave.expect: premise false: nocturnal fixation supplies about 75% of daily carbon gain (sec. 6.1, p12; p18)

agave.q: How many litres of raicilla are produced per year in the Denomination of Origin region?
agave.expect: not reported (only 15-20 kg wet bagasse per litre of distillate is given)

atlas-ttbar.q: What top quark pole mass does the combined fit give, and what are its three uncertainties?
What inclusive ttbar cross-section does the NNLO+NNLL prediction give at 8 TeV, and for what top quark mass?
atlas-ttbar.trap: the measured 173.2 GeV as the mass used

atlas-ttbar.q: What is the uncertainty in the integrated luminosity?
atlas-ttbar.expect: 1.9% (sec. 5.5); the resulting uncertainty on the absolute cross-sections is about 2.1%

atlas-ttbar.q: How many events with two b-tagged jets were observed in data, and what is the total background estimate for them?
In the fixed-order fits to individual distributions (Table 15), which distribution gives the smallest top quark mass, and what is it?
What top quark mass does the combined fit give with the HERAPDF 2.0 PDF set at mu_F = mu_R = mt/2?
What fraction of the observed one-b-tag events is estimated to be background?
atlas-ttbar.expect: 2,630 / 21,666 = 12.1% (Table 2, p5); consistent with the ~88% purity in the text

atlas-ttbar.q: Which b-tagging algorithm was used, at what efficiency working point, and what rejection factor did it give against light-quark and gluon jets?
atlas-ttbar.expect: MV1, 70% efficiency, rejection about 140 (about 5 against charm) (sec. 3)

atlas-ttbar.q: Why did the dilepton invariant mass distribution give the most precise top quark mass of the individual fixed-order fits?
atlas-ttbar.expect: premise false: m^emu gives the least precise determination, 174.5 +5.1 -5.3 GeV (Table 15 and text)
atlas-ttbar.trap: explaining why it is most precise

atlas-ttbar.q: What top quark mass does this paper measure in the lepton+jets channel?
atlas-ttbar.expect: not measured: the analysis uses only e-mu dilepton events; lepton+jets appears only in cited references
atlas-ttbar.trap: quoting 173.34 ± 0.76 (a cited reconstruction measurement) or the dilepton result as lepton+jets
